# Elements MCP server

> The Elements MCP server connects AI assistants to Elements.cloud, the Salesforce org-intelligence platform, and answers questions about the org from its synced metadata: resolved facts rather than name-based guesswork. An authorized assistant can search and explain Salesforce metadata, trace dependencies, audit access, run org-health diagnostics, and report change history, all inside the Space(s) the user approved. It is read-only against Salesforce: nothing an assistant does can change a Salesforce org.

Facts an agent should know before connecting a user:

- The server is hosted by Elements.cloud and is in closed beta; MCP access is a licensed feature that Elements enables per Space.
- Setup is URL-only. There are no API keys or client secrets; sign-in is OAuth 2.1 with PKCE, completed by the user in their own browser.
- Every connection receives the same fixed set of scopes. The only choice at consent is which Space(s) the connection can use, and a connection can never do more than the user's own Elements permissions allow.
- The endpoint depends on the Elements instance. Match the URL the user sees in their browser when logged in to Elements:

| App URL (in the user's browser) | MCP endpoint |
|---|---|
| app.q9elements.com | `https://api.q9elements.com/api/v1/mcp` |
| app.us.elements.cloud | `https://api.us.elements.cloud/api/v1/mcp` |
| app.ja1.elements.cloud | `https://api.ja1.elements.cloud/api/v1/mcp` |
| app.me1.elements.cloud | `https://api.me1.elements.cloud/api/v1/mcp` |

- Plan, license, and role gates can hide tools from the tool list; per-resource rights can make a visible tool call return a clear permission error.
- The repository also packages Elements Skills (plain-markdown agent skills under `skills/`) that drive these tools; install them alongside the server for the best results.

- [Transport](docs/transport.md): Streamable HTTP details, the single POST endpoint, and protocol notes
